title: Online IDE & Dev Tools Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Git, the command line, regex, keyboard shortcuts, and developer tooling.

questions.question: What does 'git stash' do?
options: A. Saves uncommitted changes temporarily and clears the working directory
C. Commits changes to a branch
questions.explain: git stash temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you get a clean working directory, and you can reapply them later with git stash pop.

questions.question: Which Git command shows the difference between the working directory and the last commit?
questions.explain: git diff compares the working directory against the last commit (or staged changes), showing exactly what has changed line by line.

questions.question: What regex pattern matches one or more digits?
questions.explain: The + quantifier means one or more occurrences, so \d+ matches any sequence of one or more digits.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut typically opens the terminal in VS Code?
questions.explain: Ctrl+` (backtick) is the default VS Code shortcut to toggle the integrated terminal panel open or closed.

questions.question: What does 'git rebase -i HEAD~3' allow you to do?
options: A. Interactively rewrite the last 3 commits
questions.explain: The -i flag opens an interactive editor listing the last 3 commits, letting you reorder, squash, edit, or drop them before rewriting history.

questions.question: In Linux, which command finds files by name recursively?
questions.explain: The find command with -name searches a directory tree recursively for files matching a given name pattern.

questions.question: What does the regex anchor '^' mean?
questions.explain: The caret (^) anchor matches the position at the start of a string or line, not an actual character.

questions.question: Which file permission allows execute for the owner only (numeric)?
questions.explain: 700 in octal permissions gives the owner full read, write, execute (7) while group and others get no access (0).

questions.question: What does 'git cherry-pick <commit-hash>' do?
options: A. Applies a specific commit from another branch to the current branch
questions.explain: git cherry-pick takes the changes introduced by one specific commit from another branch and reapplies them as a new commit on your current branch.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a .gitignore file?
options: B. Specifies files Git should not track
questions.explain: .gitignore lists file and directory patterns that Git should exclude from tracking, like build artifacts or dependency folders.

questions.question: Which Bash shortcut moves the cursor to the beginning of the line?
questions.explain: Ctrl+A in Bash's readline-based line editing moves the cursor to the beginning of the current line.

questions.question: In VS Code, what shortcut opens the Command Palette?
questions.explain: Ctrl+Shift+P opens VS Code's Command Palette, giving quick keyboard access to every available command and action.

questions.question: What does the regex quantifier '{3,6}' mean?
questions.explain: The {min,max} quantifier syntax {3,6} matches the preceding element repeated between 3 and 6 times, inclusive.

questions.question: What does 'chmod 755 script.sh' set?
options: A. Owner: rwx, Group: rwx, Others: rwx
B. Owner: rwx, Group: r-x, Others: r-x
C. Owner: r-x, Group: r-x, Others: r-x
D. Owner: rw-, Group: r--, Others: r--
questions.explain: 755 in octal breaks down as 7 (rwx) for owner, 5 (r-x) for group, and 5 (r-x) for others.

questions.question: Which Git workflow uses feature branches that merge into 'develop' before 'main'?
questions.explain: Gitflow uses a develop branch for integrating feature branches, which are only merged into main when preparing a release.

questions.question: What command shows who last modified each line of a file in Git?
questions.explain: git blame annotates each line of a file with the commit and author who last modified it, useful for tracing the history of a change.

questions.question: What does the Piston API (emkc.org) enable in a browser-based IDE?
questions.explain: Piston is a remote code execution engine that lets a browser-based IDE run code in many languages safely on a server, without needing local compilers.

questions.question: Which regex character class matches any whitespace?
questions.explain: \s is the regex shorthand character class that matches any whitespace character, including spaces, tabs, and newlines.

questions.question: What does 'git fetch' do compared to 'git pull'?
options: B. fetch merges and pull does not
C. fetch downloads changes but does not merge; pull fetches and merges
D. fetch only works with remote branches
questions.explain: git fetch only downloads remote commits and updates tracking branches without touching your working directory, while git pull also merges them in.

questions.question: In Bash, what does 'Ctrl+R' do?
questions.explain: Ctrl+R triggers Bash's reverse incremental search, letting you type characters to find a matching command from your history.

questions.question: What does the regex '(?:...)' create?
questions.explain: The (?:...) syntax creates a non-capturing group, which groups a pattern for quantifiers or alternation without storing it as a backreference.

questions.question: Which Git command undoes the last commit but keeps the changes staged?
questions.explain: git reset --soft HEAD~1 moves the branch pointer back one commit but leaves all changes staged, ready to be recommitted or edited.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an SSH config file (~/.ssh/config)?
options: C. Defines per-host SSH settings like user, port, and identity file
questions.explain: The SSH config file lets you define per-host connection settings, such as HostName, User, Port, and IdentityFile, so you can skip typing them each time.

questions.question: Which shortcut in most terminals pastes from the clipboard on Linux?
questions.explain: Most Linux terminal emulators reserve Ctrl+V for other functions, so Ctrl+Shift+V is used to paste from the clipboard instead.

questions.question: What does 'git tag -a v1.0 -m "Release"' do?
options: A. Creates an annotated tag with a message
C. Pushes a tag to remote
D. Lists all tags matching v1.0
questions.explain: The -a flag creates a full annotated tag object storing the tagger, date, and message, unlike a lightweight tag which is just a pointer.
